relations.subject: Ghulam Yazdani
relations.evidence: In 1903, he stood first in Aligarh Muslim University in his intermediate exams, and in 1905, he stood first in Arabic, Oriental Classics, and English in the B.A. exam

relations.subject: Ghulam Yazdani
relations.role: Epigraphist to the Government of India for Persian and Arabic inscriptions
relations.evidence: He succeeded Josef Horovitz as the Epigraphist to the Government of India for Persian and Arabic inscriptions in 1915, and held that office till 1941.

relations.subject: Ghulam Yazdani
relations.evidence: In 1907, he was appointed the Professor of Persian at St. Stephen's College in Delhi

relations.subject: Ghulam Yazdani
relations.evidence: in 1909, H. Sharp (later Sir Henry Sharp) appointed him as the Professor of Arabic in the Government College at Rajshahi in Bengal.

relations.subject: Ghulam Yazdani
relations.evidence: In 1913, the Government of Punjab appointed him as the Professor of Arabic at the Government College in Lahore.

relations.subject: Ghulam Yazdani
relations.object: Archaeological Department of H.E.H the Nizam's Dominions
relations.evidence: He became the first Director of the department and served for 30 years till his retirement in 1943.

relations.subject: Haroon Khan Sherwani
relations.evidence: Dr. Yazdani was also a mentor to the next generation of scholars who worked on the Deccan, such as Haroon Khan Sherwani.

relations.subject: Haroon Khan Sherwani
relations.evidence: Dr. Sherwani is best known for his two volume work co-edited with Purushottam Mahadev Joshi (Director, Bombay Archives) called History of Medieval Deccan.
